chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man came to a woman and asked her to marry him to herself. She said: I will marry you to myself on the condition that you seek from me whatever you wish of looking and seeking pleasure, and attain from me what a man attains from his family, except that you do not insert your private part into my private part and enjoy yourself as you wish, for I fear disgrace. He said: 'There is no harm; he has only what was stipulated.'
And there is no harm in enjoying (sexual pleasure) with the Hashimiyyah (a woman from the Banu Hashim).

key_terms.الْهَاشِمِيَّة: A woman from the Banu Hashim clan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a marriage where vaginal intercourse is explicitly excluded by the wife's condition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-shurut min al-mawdu'at* (conditions within the contract), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a marriage with a specific stipulation excluding vaginal intercourse (*al-tamattu' bi-l-dhakar*). This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital agreements, allowing spouses to define the scope of their sexual rights, while also noting the permissibility of enjoying Hashimiyyah women, a point of scholarly discussion regarding lineage or specific groups. The Imam’s declaration that 'there is no harm' (*la ba'sa*) confirms the validity of the contract as long as the condition is clear and mutually agreed upon.
